events.text: You lean over a basin to wash your face. The face in the water does not lean with you. It looks up, patient, and says in your own voice: "You are tired of holding back. So am I."

choices.text: Answer it: "Then stop holding back"

effects.log: The face smiles, and you feel your energy surge like a river let out of a dam. It is the best you have felt in years. That is what frightens you, later.

choices.text: Tip the basin out on the ground

effects.log: The water soaks into the dust. For a long while you sit with your hands on your knees and breathe, until the only face you can feel is your own.

choices.text: Look at it until it looks away first

effects.log: It takes until dawn. In the end the water is only water, and you are very tired, and a little proud.

events.text: In the hour before sleep a voice begins to recite a list: every slight, every debt, every person who ever laughed at you. It has a very good memory. It wants you to know it is keeping count.

choices.text: Listen, and add the names it forgot

effects.log: By morning the list is long and you know it by heart. You walk through the town and see a debtor on every corner.

choices.text: Recite a sutra over it, line by line

effects.log: The voice and the sutra speak at once for an hour. Then only the sutra is left, and then only your breathing.

choices.text: Write the list down and burn it

effects.log: The paper curls and goes black. It is only paper. The names were only names.

events.text: In the middle of your forms your hands move by themselves, into a shape you were never taught, and the qi follows it like a dog that has found its true master. Something inside you whispers: "Faster this way. Much faster."

choices.text: Follow the shape to its end

effects.log: The form ends with your palm an inch from the training post, and the post splits from top to bottom without being touched. You did not know you could do that. You are not sure it was you.

choices.text: Stop, and begin the forms again from the first

effects.log: The old forms are slow and clumsy after that taste of speed. You do all of them anyway, twice, until they are yours again.

choices.text: Sit down where you stand

effects.log: You sit on the cold ground of the yard with the qi thrashing in your meridians, and wait, and wait, until it remembers who it belongs to.

events.text: You dream you are walking through a town at night where everyone is asleep, and only you are awake. Nobody will ever stop you again, the dream says. Nobody will ever be able to. You wake with the feeling that it was a promise.

choices.text: Keep the promise close

effects.log: All day the dream sits behind your eyes. People step out of your way in the street and you do not notice that they are afraid.

choices.text: Go out and greet the people of the real town

effects.log: The baker, the water-carrier, a child chasing a goose. Every one of them awake, and talking, and in your way. It is wonderful.

choices.text: Tell the dream to a temple monk

effects.log: The monk listens without blinking and says only, "Good. You told it. Now it is smaller." Strangely, it is.

events.text: A temple bell rings somewhere in the hills, the plain evening bell the monks strike every day. Something in your chest flinches from the sound as if it had been struck.

choices.text: Walk towards the bell

effects.log: You climb the hill path in the dusk. Each stroke hurts a little less. By the time you reach the gate it is only a bell again.

choices.text: Cover your ears and walk the other way

effects.log: The bell fades behind you. The thing in your chest settles, pleased, and purrs like a cat that has been fed.

choices.text: Count the strokes and breathe with them

effects.log: One hundred and eight strokes, one hundred and eight breaths. At the end your hands have stopped shaking.

events.text: In the market a small child looks up at your face, goes white, and runs behind a stall. The child's mother apologises, flustered. "Children," she says. "They see things that are not there."

choices.text: Smile, and buy the child a sweet

effects.log: The child takes the sweet from behind the mother's skirt, very carefully, and then smiles back. You keep that smile for the rest of the year.

choices.text: Look into a shop window to see what the child saw

effects.log: For a moment the face in the glass is not quite yours, and not quite a face. You decide you like it.

choices.text: Leave the market and do not come back for a while

effects.log: You walk out of town and sit on a riverbank until your face feels like your own again.

events.text: You are drinking tea with an old acquaintance, talking of nothing, when you notice your free hand has already settled on the hilt of your weapon. You do not remember moving it. Your acquaintance has noticed too.

choices.text: Take your hand away and laugh it off

effects.log: You laugh. After a moment your acquaintance laughs too, a little too loudly. You pour the next cup with both hands.

choices.text: Leave your hand where it is

effects.log: The talk dries up. Your acquaintance finds a reason to leave early, and does not look back at the door.

choices.text: Tell the truth: "Something in me wants a fight"

effects.log: Your acquaintance is quiet, then refills your cup. "Then we will just drink until it gets bored," they say, and you do.

events.text: The voice is very reasonable tonight. "One memory," it says. "Only one. The day you were happiest. Give it to me and I will give you strength enough that nobody can ever take anything from you again."

choices.text: Give it the memory

effects.log: You do not remember what you gave. You only know that something warm is gone, and your energy is deep and cold and very strong.

choices.text: Hold the memory tighter

effects.log: You hold it all night: the light, the voices, the smell of that day. By dawn the voice has gone quiet and the memory is brighter than it was.

choices.text: Ask the voice what it is really afraid of

effects.log: It does not answer. That is an answer. You sleep better than you have in months.
